I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child with a 3-week history of fatigue, easy bruising, fever, and severe leg pain. To understand your condition, have you noticed if your gums bleed when you brush, or if you have any tiny red spots on your skin?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.
REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.1 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count: 63,000/mm3 (elevated), Platelet_Count: 27,000/mm3 (decreased), Bone_Marrow_Aspirate: Predominantly immature cells that are positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work and bone marrow aspirate are highly concerning for acute lymphoblastic leukemia, given the high white blood cell count, low platelets, and the presence of immature cells (blasts) expressing CD10, CD19, and TdT. Before I make a final diagnosis, have you noticed any bone pain specifically in your hips, shoulders, or knees, or any swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpits?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)
